title: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

sense.text: “And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.” Ham was the youngest son of Noah and one of the eight persons who lived through the flood. He became the progenitor of the dark races, but he is not the father of the Negroes: the Egyptians, Ethiopians, Libyans (not the modern ones you see today) and the Canaanites. The sons of Ham are the Hamites, the Nilotes. The Ishmaelites, the people of Ishmael, are the Arabs, a totally different race of people. The Arabs are not the ancient Egyptians nor Libyans, and the Caucasians are not the Jews, the children of Israel.

precepts.why: Were the ancient Egyptians Arabs or were they Hamites the way the Bible says? “Israel also came into Egypt; and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.” Egypt is the land of Ham, meaning the Hamites, the Nilotes. The books on ancient Egypt show it: the slaves rowing the boats, the Pharaoh and his family, Queen Nefertari, Tutankhamun, dark brown people in Egypt. They sure don’t look like those Arabs. The ancient Egyptian pharaohs were black; they were Hamites, Nilotes, but they were not the Negroes.

sense.text: “Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord”. We’re the ones saved by the Lord. People talk about they saved; the only ones saved by the Lord are the Israelites, the 12 tribes. That’s the prophecy right there. “And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee”: we’re going to uncover a lot of lies today. “And thou shalt tread upon their high places”: we’re going to rule them, we’re going to dominate them.
This occurred during the time of Nebuchadnezzar. When Nebuchadnezzar smote Egypt, the true Egyptians, the sons and daughters of Ham, were scattered, but after 40 years they came back to the land.

“And they shall be there a base kingdom.” Base is the root word of basement; you can get no lower, that’s the bottom. At one time ancient Egypt was the world’s superpower. The Lord said after Nebuchadnezzar smote them they would never rise again: “for I will diminish them, that they shall no more rule over the nations.” Kemet is just another word for Ham; when they say they’re Kemet, that’s Hamitic.

“And it shall be no more the confidence of the house of Israel”. When Nebuchadnezzar was going to come against us, our forefathers made a league with Egypt to help fight ancient Babylon, and that got wiped out; we got wiped out and Egypt got wiped out. The Lord had warned us through Jeremiah not to make a league with Egypt. Some of our people today believe Egypt is on the rise, but those ancient Egyptians you can’t even find today. Egypt was conquered by the Muslim Arabs in 641 A.D., the Ottoman Turks took over in 1517, and Turkish rule ended around 1952 when Gamal Abdel Nasser came to power. The modern Egyptians are Arabs, Ishmaelites, not Hamites at all.

“So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.” When you read about the coffins in the Bible, this is what it’s talking about: like the cedar coffin of Ramses II. America didn’t come up with the concept of a coffin; they got it from ancient Egypt, and the embalming America does they got from ancient Egypt. That is not the Israelite custom; that’s what was done in ancient Egypt.

“They search out iniquities”: the white man searches out iniquities; they’re archaeologists. “They accomplish a diligent search”: when they dig, if it takes months or years, they discover whole civilizations, and they get paid hundreds of thousands if not millions of dollars to do these digs. Many of the tombs were underground in the sand; they had to dig it all up and search out the iniquities of ancient Egypt, and many of the sins they discovered in Egypt they incorporated here in the United States of America: the obelisk, and the trinity of Isis, Osiris and their son, where they get the Father, Son and Holy Ghost from.

The scholars know it. In the 1840s Morton showed from mummy heads and tomb inscriptions that the Egyptians were not Negroes, and that blacks had been relegated to the same servile position in ancient Egypt as in modern America. It was the Israelites as slaves in ancient Egypt, and it’s the Israelite slavery here in America. “Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs”, referring to Egypt, “and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years”.

precepts.why: “Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”: a new dynasty, Ahmose the first. “Come on, let us deal wisely with them”: deal wisely meant enslave us. They didn’t want us to join with their enemies to overthrow them. “They built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses”: it was under Ramses the second that we made the Exodus. “But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew”: we don’t die, we multiply. “And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour”: rigor is going into slavery.

“Therefore the king of Egypt rose up against them, and dealt subtilly with them, and brought them low with labouring in brick, and made them slaves.” They made us slaves; in case Exodus wasn’t clear for you, Judith makes it clear. The Pictorial History of Israel has a mural from the Theban tomb of Rekhmire, vizier in the time of Thutmose the third, depicting Israel’s bondage in Egypt. Look at Israel; these are not Arabs or Caucasians. The scholars know that the ancient Israelites were black people.

“Put off thy shoes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest is holy ground”: none of that Egyptian philosophy up here. “I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt”, and remember Egypt is in Africa. Harper’s Bible Dictionary shows the frescoes from the synagogue at Dura-Europos depicting Moses three times leading the ancient Israelites out of Egypt: look at the afros on Moses, and the hand of God, black hands that look like Moses, that look like the Israelites. The ancient Egyptians were black and the ancient Israelites were black, but although they were black they were two different races. The Egyptians are Hamites, the Nilotes; the Israelites are Shemites. That’s who we are.

sense.text: “And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. They thought Moses was an Egyptian. Why? Because they look similar. They mistook Moses for an Egyptian.

precepts.why: “Art not thou that Egyptian”: they took the apostle Paul for a Hamite, an Egyptian. “But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew”: I’m not a Hamite, I’m not Egyptian. Tarsus is located in Turkey; Paul was born in Turkey. “A citizen of no mean city” means he didn’t come from the ghetto; Paul came from a well-to-do family. Moses was an Israelite mistaken for an Egyptian; Paul was an Israelite mistaken for an Egyptian. How in the hell you gonna look at them reading the Torah and mistake them for ancient Egyptians? Impossible.

sense.text: “I know thy works”: we worked hard. “And tribulation”: we catch hell in this country. “And poverty”: we are an impoverished people because we’re under Edomite domination. “(but thou art rich)”: all the promises in the Bible pertain to our people, our 12 tribes. “And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” Jesus Christ called them the devil. They’re frauds. The Bible speaks it; we didn’t write this.

precepts.why: Here’s the precept that goes with that; this pertains to them. “We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”: these people are counterfeits, fakes, frauds, phony. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness”: we abstain from their ways as from filthiness, because they don’t do nothing but study the Talmud and lie. “He pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”: our end is going to be blessed, “and maketh his boast that God is his father”: God is our father. Don’t be ashamed of the word of God. Christ said if you’re ashamed of me before men I’ll be ashamed of you before my Father and the angels which are in heaven.

sense.text: “Wisdom hath builded her house”: wisdom, this Bible. “She hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Those are the seven attributes all of us must attain to. Wherever we’ve fallen short we better pray for that, meditate and study to attain it; pray to the Lord that he endow us with those seven pillars of wisdom.

precepts.why: Isaiah 11 talks about Christ, and these are the seven pillars. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”: pillar number one, the spirit of the Lord, the Holy Spirit. “The spirit of wisdom”: pillar two. “And understanding”: three. “The spirit of counsel”: four. “And might”: five. “The spirit of knowledge”: six. “And of the fear of the Lord”: seven. It starts off that you must have the Holy Spirit on you.
“Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.” Christ is the wisdom of God; that’s why we talk about the seven pillars of wisdom.

sense.text: “I say the truth in Christ, I lie not”: Paul says I’m not lying at all; the Holy Ghost is on me, that’s who’s speaking through me. “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”: I wish I could take all the curses of Deuteronomy 28 on me so that my brothers, my kinsmen, wouldn’t have to go through this. Christians like to run from that word the flesh, but he’s going to break it down for us.

“Who are Israelites”: the Israelites are Paul’s kinsmen according to the flesh, not all nations on the planet. “To whom pertaineth” means to whom belongeth: the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God and the promises. You know the churches hate Romans chapter 9; it gives you God’s plan perfectly, just like Daniel 7.

“Whose are the fathers”: the fathers of this record called the Bible. “And of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came”. When you’re on the street breaking this down, don’t let the dumb Christian run past that, because they go spiritual Israel. You got to stress it: as concerning the flesh Christ came.

precepts.why: What is the adoption? “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law”. That’s not all nations on the planet Earth. All nations were not under the law of God; he gave the law to Moses, who gave it to the 12 tribes of Israel, “that we might receive the adoption of sons.” So that only pertains to the 12 tribes of Israel.

What is the glory? “Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” David is saying that because we have not been joyful in our King. The way we’re joyful in our King is by keeping his laws, his commandments, his high holy days, but our people have been joyful in Christmas, in Kwanzaa, in Ramadan. “Let the saints be joyful in glory”: glory is the Kingdom of Heaven, “To execute vengeance upon the heathen, and punishments upon the people”.

The covenants. “For finding fault with them”: with the Israelites. “I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”, because we were split into two kingdoms. “Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers”: the end of animal sacrifice. “And I regarded them not”: we went into slavery for breaking God’s first covenant. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: this is the New Covenant.
The giving of the law. “For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel”. The law was not for all nations on the planet Earth.
The service of God: who gave the service unto God? “For unto me the children of Israel are servants”. Not all nations on the planet Earth are the servants of God.

The promises. “Of this man’s seed”, of David’s seed, of David’s sperm, “hath God according to his promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus”. The promises are made to Israel, not all nations on the planet Earth.

Whose are the fathers of this record called the Bible? “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail”: none of the promises in the Bible shall fail. “None shall want her mate”: you can’t mate the Bible with no other book. “For my mouth it hath commanded”: God’s mouth commanded the writings of this record. “And his spirit it hath gathered them”: God’s spirit collected these writings together. “And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line”: Jeremiah got a lot, Ezekiel got a lot, Obadiah got one chapter, Jude got one chapter. “They shall possess it for ever”: we’re going to possess the book and the land forever.
“Ye men of Israel, hear these words; Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs”.

“Therefore being a prophet”: referring to King David. “That of the fruit of his loins”: you got to slow it down there. His loins is making reference to his penis; the fruit is what comes out of his penis. “According to the flesh”: in case you doubt it, not spiritual, according to the flesh, “he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”. There’s no immaculate conception, there’s no virgin birth at all. When you’re on the street read verses like this slow, because Christianity is worse than crack; it has drugged our entire nation of people.

sense.text: “Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect”, because the word of God is taking effect. Did we go into slavery? Were our families destroyed and decimated? Are there earthquakes in diverse places, pestilence, wars and rumors of wars? The Bible is taking effect. “For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel”: all Israelites are not going to repent.

precepts.why: “Then certain ungodly persons, who hated their own people”. Those are your Uncle Ruckus, people like Stephen in Django, and believe me they are around today. Some of them are your church ministers, some of them your congressmen, your assemblymen.

“Know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God?” Enmity is hatred with God. “Whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world”: like we read in Maccabees, you want to be a friend with the Greeks, the Romans, America, “is the enemy of God.”

“But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy”: they saw the multitudes of people who wanted to repent. The root of envy is hatred. “Contradicting and blaspheming”: that’s what we see today on the street. You’ll be out there teaching and here come a Christian out of nowhere to contradict and blaspheme everything you bring out. Before you brothers got on the street that damn Christian wasn’t teaching a damn thing, but he saw you getting a crowd.

“Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven”: that’s the brothers and sisters that legitimately repent. “But the children of the kingdom”: the scribes, the Pharisees, those religious men and women, “shall be cast out into outer darkness”, because they never wanted to accept Christ as Savior and keep the commandments. It was true back then and it’s true today.

sense.text: “Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children”: just because you come from Abraham’s lineage does not make you children of God. Abraham had Ishmael by Hagar and six sons by Keturah. “But, In Isaac shall thy seed be called”: the Lord is saying, I’m not calling all of them; I’m calling the one Sarah had. That’s the boy I’m dealing with.

“They which are the children of the flesh”: now he’s expanding the thought. The children of the flesh are all the other nations: “these are not the children of God”. Christians say everybody are the children of God, but these are not the children of God. “But the children of the promise are counted for the seed”: the children that came from Isaac.
“For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son.” He’s breaking it down in case you’re still confused about the children of the promise.

precepts.why: “And Hagar bare Abram a son: and Abram called his son’s name, which Hagar bare, Ishmael.” Abram was 86 years old when Hagar bare Ishmael to him.
“And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.” Isaac was born to Abraham and Sarah.

“Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.” This is after Sarah died; Abraham married a younger woman named Keturah, “And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah”: six sons.

“In Isaac shall thy seed be called” is the prophecy. “Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy bondwoman”: don’t worry about Ishmael and Hagar, the Lord said. Sarah had said that bond boy ain’t gonna be heir with my son. It was a heated moment, but although she was angry the spirit was on her. “In all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice”: the Lord had to remind Abraham, you might be mad at her, but what she said was of me; it was correct. Isaac’s the chosen seed.
“Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called”. Israel is the Lord’s called.

Here’s the precept to prove the children of the flesh are not the children of God. “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket”: if you’re walking with a bucket of water and a drop falls out, you don’t give a damn about that drop; God’s comparing the nations to that drop. “And are counted as the small dust of the balance”: how much does small dust weigh on a balance? Nothing. “Behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing”. “And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn”: if they wanted to sacrifice to be God’s people, it’s not sufficient. “All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity”: vanity means a waste of time.

Isn’t Israel included in that? No. “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people”: God told Isaiah to comfort the Israelites. “Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned”. Some of the comfortable words God says to tell us are that the nations are as nothing. That makes us feel good inside, because at one time you might think God’s dealing with other nations. That’s Bible, people; but that makes you uncomfortable, because your church has never taught you that.

“Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.” The everlasting covenant was with Isaac, Sarah’s son, not all nations on the planet Earth, and not the other children that Abraham had either.

sense.text: “But when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac”: so Rebecca and Isaac had more than one child.

“For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil”: before they were born, they didn’t do anything good, they didn’t do anything evil. “That the purpose of God according to election might stand”: God was doing the choosing. “Not of works, but of him that calleth”: it had nothing to do with them doing anything good or evil; it was God’s decision. I’m going to choose one to love and one to hate, and he made his decision before they were born.

“The elder shall serve the younger”: the elder boy is destined to be a slave to the younger. “Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” That was done before they were born. It had nothing to do with Esau selling his birthright; God already chose Jacob and already hated Esau. When you brothers are teaching it, don’t let a Christian befuddle you.

precepts.why: “And Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren”. “And the children struggled together within her”: children, plural. “Two nations are in thy womb”: Genesis means beginning; this is the beginning of two different nations. “And two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”: two different types of people, separated, not assimilated, not integrated. “And the one people shall be stronger than the other people”, able to endure great hardships, “and the elder shall serve the younger”: that’s about the kingdom on Earth. These were not identical twins, they were fraternal twins. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau”: the blood showed through his skin. It gave Esau’s color but did not give Jacob’s, because Jacob looked just like Isaac and Rebecca, like all the people from Genesis 2 on up; everybody was melanated until this character Esau came on the scene. “Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.” “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”: that same red, because it looked like him. “Therefore was his name called Edom”: Edom means red, so you’ll read his name as Esau or Edom. A Nigerian couple had one black boy and one albino-looking boy; they come from us, we don’t come from Caucasians.

Where was it written? “The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi. I have loved you, saith the Lord.” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau”. That’s some cold stuff right there. Churches don’t want to deal with it; they don’t want you to identify Esau, and you got some Israelite communities that don’t want to identify these demons as Esau. That’s exactly who the Caucasian man and woman is.

sense.text: People say y’all are filled with hate. No, it has nothing to do with hatred; we’re reading the Bible. We’re the prophets of the Most High God, and our job is to tell you the truth. “Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.” Somebody will say it’s not right for God to hate Esau. God made his decision; he’s God and you’re not. Paul is giving you a brief synopsis of God’s plan from Genesis; that’s what this whole chapter is about.

“I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.” As it was true back then, when the Lord had mercy on Israel in the captivity under Egypt, Paul is bringing it up to his time. “So then it is not of him that willeth”: Esau can’t will himself to be the people of God, can’t will himself to be the Israelites. “Nor of him that runneth”: you can run around the earth, church after church, synagogue after synagogue, and say I’m a Christian, I’m the people of God. “But of God that sheweth mercy”: it’s God’s decision who he’s going to have mercy on.

precepts.why: Paul is explaining the whole plan of God to us. “Declaring the end from the beginning”: from the Genesis God declared the end. “Saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”: I’m going to do what I want to do; mankind, you have nothing to say.

“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”. Why will he yet choose Israel? Because we broke the covenant, we broke God’s laws, but he had prophesied he would send a Savior. “And the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: other nations are going to obey us. “For servants and handmaids”: that’s the elder shall serve the younger from Genesis 25, and we have yet to come to that. “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” “In the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”: that’s what Christ said, come unto me all ye that labor and are heavy laden and I will give you rest. We are waiting on that day.

sense.text:
Why did Paul go from Jacob and Esau to Moses and Pharaoh? He’s comparing Jacob and Esau to Egypt, bringing it up to his time, when the Israelites were under Roman domination. “Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up”: did not God raise up Pharaoh to be the world’s superpower? In Paul’s time the world’s superpower was Rome, and today it’s the United States of America. America is the new Pharaoh; Esau Edom is the new Pharaoh. The book Modern Judaism (1830) says ‘the descendants of Esau the sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob even to the end of the world’, that they ‘subjugated Italy, founded Rome and the Roman Empire’, ‘professing the religion of Jesus of Nazareth’, and ‘hold the dominion over all Europe’. The scholars know Esau is Rome, and that the prophecies against Edom in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Obadiah have not yet received their full accomplishment.

“That I might shew my power in thee”: he would raise Esau up to such a level only God can take him down, just as when we were in Egypt only God could take down ancient Egypt. There are roughly 750 U.S. military bases outside of America, spread across 80 nations, three times as many as all other countries combined, with combatant commands in Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Indo-Pacific. That’s why when black people say let’s get guns and overthrow them, be quiet; you ain’t overthrowing nothing. Their military has worldwide coverage. “And that my name might be declared throughout all the earth”: everybody is going to declare the name throughout the whole earth.

precepts.why: “And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast”: the ten horns are the European Union. “These shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire”: this place is going to be burnt up with fire. “For God hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will”: God put in the hearts of the European Union to burn America down, “until the words of God shall be fulfilled”: when our time of prophesying is up, that’s when it’s going to go down. “And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth”: that’s the United States of America. Based on that, do you think America’s finished yet? Oh no.

“And thou, Asia, that art partaker of the hope of Babylon”: Asia wants to be like America, particularly China and Japan. There are 48 countries in Asia, and China, India and Pakistan have nuclear arms. “Because thou hast made thyself like unto her”: you made yourself like America. “And hast decked thy daughters in whoredom”: the daughters are their companies, their corporations. “Thy lovers, which have always desired to commit whoredom with thee”: they always desire to do business with America.

“And in the passage they shall rush on the idle city”: the idle city here is Asia, and the European Union shall rush on it. “And shall destroy some portion of thy land, and consume part of thy glory”: some portions of China and Japan shall be destroyed. “And shall return to Babylon that was destroyed”: the U.S. military shall return to Babylon that was destroyed. Although this place is destroyed, they’re coming back. Their military is not finished during this war. The EU is going to burn up this place, but the Lord said, I’m the only one that can take down Babylon the great.

Examples of God showing his power. “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies”. “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: that’s the mushroom cloud, the Armageddon explosion. “And all their host shall fall down”: their missiles, their satellites, their jets, their bombers, everything in the air. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”: Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. It includes the European Union and the remnants of Babylon the great, the United States of America, all them bases they got; the Lord said I’m the only one that can take them down. “And upon the people of my curse”: Edom is the people of God’s curse.

“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered”: talking about the daughter of Babylon. That’s what we do when we prophesy on the streets; we’re uncovering their nakedness. They’re not a Christian nation, they’re not the Jews. “Sit on the ground: there is no throne”: your kingdom is finished. “For thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”: you shall no more be called Christian or Jewish. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man”: when Christ returns he said I’m not coming back in that weak form you put a crown of thorns on and nailed to the cross; I’ma meet you as God. Only the Lord can take down Babylon, 100 percent.

“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” “Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel”: why does it look like grape juice is all on your clothes, Lord? “I have trodden the winepress alone”: the winepress is the Earth. “And of the people there was none with me”: of the Israelites there was none to help; God didn’t need your help. “For I will tread them in mine anger”: verse one tells you who; Edom is America, Edom is the EU, France, Germany. “And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”: the wine Isaiah thought it was is blood. “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.”

“And the ten horns which thou sawest are ten kings, which have received no kingdom as yet”: the EU, during the time of John the Revelator. “These have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast”: they’re going to give their economic and military power to support America for one hour. “These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them”: Christ the Son of God shall overcome them.

“And in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” Who said Christ is coming back to hug and kiss everybody? He’s coming back to make war. “And the armies which were in heaven followed him”: there’s armies in heaven coming with the Son of God. “And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations”: that sharp sword is the word, the law of God. “And I saw an angel standing in the sun”: you know Mary didn’t have sex with no doggone angel. “And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse”: the beast goes into the EU and the American remnant. That’s what we read in Isaiah 34 and Isaiah 63. “And with him the false prophet”: the whole church system. “Them that had received the mark of the beast”: everybody that follows the policies of America; their policies are sin, religiously or politically, and it takes you away from God’s laws.

“He neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war: But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire”. “And fell with violence upon the multitude which was prepared to fight”: the EU, the remnants of the United States of America and all their military bases, India, Japan, China, all of them nations. “And when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled”: imagine the King of Kings coming down upon the Earth and everything trembles in fear. “Were sore afraid, and yet durst fight”: remember when the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart to make him chase the children of Israel so he could destroy his army. The same thing is going to happen in these last days; he’s hardening Esau’s heart against us. That’s why in places like Mississippi they’re trying to create Jim Crow laws. Some of you think you got some good white folk friends.

“The same is he whom God the Highest hath kept a great season”. “And he shall order them that are left behind”: he’s going to order the Israelites that are left behind. “Behold, the days come, when the most High will begin to deliver them that are upon the earth”. “And then shall my Son be declared”: this is Christ. All the nations are going to be fighting each other, Christ is going to interrupt their fighting, then they all gonna turn against him. “Like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands”: that’s talking about the 12 tribes of Israel. “And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations”: their military, their jets, their ICBM missiles mean nothing to the Lord. “And he shall destroy them without labour by the law”: the law is fire coming out of the Son of God’s mouth.

“Behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire”. God said his words are like fire, a spiritual fire. But when the Son of God comes back, God’s word is going to be literal fire when he starts speaking the laws to these nations.

sense.text: “Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy”: meaning Israel, Jacob. “And whom he will he hardeneth”: he’s going to harden Esau. Paul is still on the same topic. He speaks with words hard to be understood, and Christians go, why’d he start talking about Jacob and Esau, Esau have I hated, then go to Pharaoh? He’s letting you know Esau would be the new Pharaoh.

precepts.why: Who is he going to have mercy on? We read Isaiah 14:1-3 already; here’s another precept about mercy. “He hath holpen his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy”: on Israel, not all nations on the planet Earth.

sense.text: “For who hath resisted his will?” Everybody does what God wants. “Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God?” Who in the hell are you to reply against your maker, your creator, with your ashy lips? “Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” How could Esau jump up now and go, why have you made me this way? And some of our own people, when we say you’re the greatest nation on Earth, go no, we gotta be like everybody else; but God says you’re the top.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour”: out of Rebecca he made two. One vessel unto honour, which was Jacob, “and another unto dishonour”: that vessel is Esau.

“The vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”: fitted means created to be destroyed. We already read in Isaiah 34 that his sword will come down upon Idumea, the people of his curse, and in Isaiah 63, who is this that cometh from Edom with dyed garments.
“That he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”: that’s Israel, “which he had afore prepared unto glory”.

precepts.why: Who’s the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction? “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble”. “And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” That’s it right there.

“The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war”. “He shall prevail against his enemies.” “I have long time holden my peace”: I sat back quiet for centuries. “I have been still, and refrained myself”: refrained from intervening for the Israelites. “Now will I cry like a travailing woman”: I’m going to scream like a woman in childbirth pains. “I will destroy and devour at once”: he’s talking about the nations. “I will make waste mountains and hills”: governments and smaller governments.

Here’s a precept that he afore prepared us unto glory. “Now will I bring again the captivity of Jacob”: he’s going to bring us back to the land, “and have mercy upon the whole house of Israel, and will be jealous for my holy name”. “After that they have borne their shame”: right now we’re bearing the shame of breaking God’s laws. “When they dwelt safely in their land, and none made them afraid”: back in the day in our land none made us afraid. “And gathered them out of their enemies’ lands”: today we’re in our enemies’ lands. “Which caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen”: we’re going to have learned our lesson. “And have left none of them any more there”: no Israelites are going to be left in the enemy’s land; that’s what Isaiah 14:1-2 was saying. “For I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel”: that’s the Holy Spirit.

sense.text: Now Paul is going to break down the mercy, because the argument was the northern kingdom don’t get no mercy, because they were not doing animal sacrifice. “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only, “but also of the Gentiles”. That throws Christians off right there; some of y’all Christians are sitting there going, gotcha. But the Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel. The scattered remnants of Israel and Judah are going to be gathered together.

precepts.why: “In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated”: all of us, when we repent, have already been predestinated, “according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will”: according to the Most High God. “That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ.”

The Gentiles that were called. “It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”: to you Jews. “But seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.”

Here’s the prophecy about Acts 13:46. “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The Jews had to hear the word first, so that the other tribes don’t try to overtake them.
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. So Zebulun and Naphtali were called Gentiles.

Anytime you go to Isaiah 11, start at verse 10; there’s a reason. “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse”: that root of Jesse is Christ, “which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek”. You want to stress that. Christ already ascended on high, so the ensign today is the Bible. “The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. “And shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” It explains that the Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel; that’s why you start with verse 10, where it stipulates Gentiles.

sense.text: “As he saith also in Osee”: Osee is the Greek for Hosea. “I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.” Paul is quoting the prophet Hosea, and Christians don’t like to go to the quotes because they get cut.
“There shall they be called the children of the living God.” Paul is quoting Hosea about Israel.

precepts.why: “And I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy”: because it sure looked like we had not obtained mercy; that’s what slavery seemed like. “And I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.”

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea”: the children of Israel. “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”: it was said we’re not God’s people; we’re called by Gentile names, African-American, Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican and so forth. “There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” We are the sons of the living God.

sense.text: “Esaias also crieth concerning Israel”: Esaias is the Greek for Isaiah. “Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved”. Only a remnant of our people is going to be saved, brothers and sisters, only a remnant.
“For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.” The Lord is going to make a short work on this Earth.

precepts.why: Paul is quoting Isaiah. “For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return”: because they are not all Israel which are of Israel, all Israel is not going to repent; a remnant of us shall repent. “The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.”

“Go, and ye shall receive: pray for few days unto you, that they may be shortened: the kingdom is already prepared for you: watch.” Brothers and sisters, the kingdom’s already prepared; it’s already done.
“And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.”

sense.text: “And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed”: Sabaoth is the transliteration of the Hebrew word meaning hosts, armies, the Lord of armies or Lord of hosts. If the Lord didn’t leave a seed of Israelites to repent, all of us “had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.” I know it’s a hard thing, but the word of God is meant for them to repent.

precepts.why: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: the great city is the United States of America, “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. This ain’t the real Sodom, but this is a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt. “Where also our Lord was crucified”: his image was crucified and his teachings were crucified here.
That’s the prophecy Paul quotes: “Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.”

“The shew of their countenance doth witness against them”, and this is talking about Israelites. “And they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not”: wicked Israelites don’t try to hide it no more. “Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.” The pictures witness against them: men in makeup, in wigs, in the gully. That’s Benjamin, that’s Ephraim. You Puerto Ricans thought you was gonna escape; you ain’t escaping, and you Dominicans don’t escape either, with your nasty behinds.

“Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush”: Israelites couldn’t even blush. “Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths”: that’s talking about this Bible. “Where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.” “But they said, We will not walk therein”: you hear what our people said; we ain’t walking in them old paths.

Some say those Israelites could never repent; that’s not true. “Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind”: that’s the homosexual right there, and the effeminate, brothers that cross their legs like a woman like you ain’t got nothing down there. “And such were some of you”: that’s the point right there. “But ye are washed”: you repented, “but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.” Repentance is open to all of our people.

sense.text: We know who these Gentiles are according to Matthew 4:15 and Isaiah 11:10-12: the scattered Israelites, the outcasts of Israel, the dispersed of Judah. “The Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness”: those scattered Israelites were not brought up under the law of Moses and never heard about Christ; they were raised up under Gentile philosophies, Greek and Roman, just like our people today brought up under American Christian philosophies and Islamic philosophies. “Have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith”: which is Christ. The apostles and disciples went out teaching those Israelites scattered abroad.

“But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness”: those scribes, Pharisees and Sadducees brought up under the law of Moses. Brought up to today, those are the religious ones, our people brought up under Christianity and Islam. “Hath not attained to the law of righteousness”: they did not understand the law in Christ.
“Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law”: to get salvation, animal sacrifice. “For they stumbled at that stumblingstone”.

“Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence”: I lay in Israel a stumbling stone which is Christ, and he also is that rock of offence. “And whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.” Brothers and sisters, we ain’t gonna be ashamed. The Bible says we win at the end of all this; that’s what Romans 9 is explaining. But to win we must believe; we must prepare to win and expect to win.

precepts.why: “I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarry: and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory.” Salvation is for Israel, his glory.

“For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness”: initially the scribes, Sadducees and Pharisees. Brought up to today: I will celebrate white Jesus on Christmas, Valentine’s Day, Thanksgiving, Mother’s Day; another group goes to the Wailing Wall and humps it. They “have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.” “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness”: the end of what law? Animal sacrifice; you can read about that in Hebrews 10. “Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven?” means you don’t believe that Christ ascended; “Who shall descend into the deep?” means you don’t believe he died for us. “That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.” All Israel has to repent. That don’t just mean say Jesus Christ and you good; it’s talking about true, sincere repentance.

What did those scribes, Pharisees and Sadducees do? “The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.” They rejected Christ, they killed Christ the Son of God, just like our people today reject the black Messiah and his teachings of keeping God’s commandments.

A Christian always tries to be slick: we don’t got to keep the commandments. Go to the last book of the Bible, the last chapter: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” That’s the only way you’re getting into New Jerusalem. Anybody that tells you you don’t got to keep the commandments, you better head for the hills.

What does it mean, they stumbled at that stumbling stone? “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. He’s the leader, he’s the king, he’s the Lord.

“And he shall be for a sanctuary”: talking about Christ, “but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel”. Many people are offended that they got to keep the commandments, that women can’t dress like men nor men like women; they are offended at the way Christ is described in the Bible, hair like wool and skin like it burns in a furnace. “And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken”: many among the Israelites shall stumble at the teachings of Christ. “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples”: disciple means student; if we are students of Christ we must seal the law in our minds.

“To whom coming, as unto a living stone”: Christ is that living stone, “disallowed indeed of men”: rejected, “but chosen of God, and precious”. “Ye also, as lively stones”: every Israelite man and woman, “are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood”. “Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone”: a leader of the people. “And he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.” “The stone which the builders disallowed”: the builders were the scribes and Pharisees, and today they’re your church leaders and your black and Latino politicians. They were supposed to build us up but they’ve done a horrible job. “The same is made the head of the corner”: Christ is made the leader. “Being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed”: they’re all appointed to fall.

“The stone which the builders rejected”. Just like you build up your child to manhood or womanhood, these leaders were supposed to build us up as a people to a proud and mighty nation, and these church leaders and politicians have failed. “The same is become the head of the corner”: regardless that they rejected Christ, he’s still the leader, the King, the Lord. “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof”: the fruits are the commandments. “But on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder”: whosoever Christ shall fall on, he shall kill.
